text:
jess_support: FYI customer AcmeCorp can't view audit logs, hitting 403. Root cause looks auth/entitlement. Details below.

AcmeCorp (org: acme-123) user: alice@acme.com says 'Audit logs page shows "You don't have permission to view audit logs."'
Error: 403 Forbidden - missing_entitlement: "audit:read". Screenshot: https://acme.screenshots/123 (customer-provided)
Steps to repro:
1) SSO login via Okta -> user lands in org
2) Navigate Console -> Settings -> Audit Logs
3) Page returns 403 and empty table

Can someone with identity knowledge pls check SAML/SCIM role mapping? @ivan_identity

omar_cs: I've tried to repro with a test Okta account mapped to the same groups. I see the same 403. Quick dump from console logs:
``
GET /api/v1/orgs/acme-123/auditlogs 403 {"error":"missing_entitlement","required":"audit:read","present":[]}
```
Customer says they used to have access last week. No recent changes on their side per their admin.

ivan_identity: looking. Two quick things: okta app is sending groups in `groups` claim, and our SAML mapping expects `appRoles` or `entitlements`. If SCIM sync doesn't include the entitlement attribute, user won't get audit:read. Asking customer to paste SAML Response (redact PII) or confirm SCIM payload. Also checking recent SCIM sync logs.

audit-bot: SCIM sync for acme-123 last successful: 2025-11-18T02:13:05Z. Last full sync size: 47 users. No errors logged. (bot)

kate_sre: could also be scope-based token problem for Console->API calls. When UI calls /auditlogs, frontend attaches session token scoped to `console:read` only. If the session token was minted without `audit:read` (OIDC scope omitted), you'll see this 403. We should check auth-server logs for token scopes for alice@acme.com at login time.

ivan_identity: found an edge: our SAML attribute mapping had been updated 3 days ago to map `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:entitlements` -> `entitlements` claim. But Okta didn't send that attribute for this user because group membership mapping uses SCIM, not the attribute. So user ended up with role 'user' only.
Suggested fix: add appRole mapping in Okta to include `audit:read` for acme-admin-group, or enable SCIM push for the relevant group membership. @acmecorp-admin can you confirm SCIM push is enabled for the Okta application?

acmecorp-admin: confirmed SCIM push is off for now (we were avoiding auto-provisioning). We can enable it but need guidance — worried about unintended role changes.

jess_support: temporary workaround: we can create a time-limited support API key scoped to `audit:read` and share via secure channel so they can download exports while they update IdP. If they want manual export we can also run an ad-hoc export and upload to their S3. Which do they prefer? @acmecorp-admin

acmecorp-admin: please create a temporary API key that'll let our security team pull audit logs. Prefer 24h key.

omar_cs: creating support ticket SUP-4982, generating scoped key. Key created with metadata: org=acme-123, scope=[audit:read], TTL=24h. Pasting a masked token: `redwood_key_***************c3f`. Delivery: sent via 1:1 secure-message. :lock: Let me know when they confirm download.

ivan_identity: For a long-term fix, recommend either:
- Enable SCIM group push for Okta app and ensure SCIM includes `entitlements` or appRole mapping for `audit:read`
- Or add a SAML app role mapping to translate Okta group `acme-auditors` into the `audit:read` entitlement
I've attached sample SAML attribute mapping for Okta:
``
SAML attribute: Entitlements -> appRoles
value: audit:read
```
Also sample Okta group assignment rule.

kate_sre: I've added a small telemetry check to auth-server to log sessions where UI request to /auditlogs fails due to missing scope and include token id for tracing. Will roll in next 10m. Hopefully gives us a clearer signal if this recurs. :eyes: 

acmecorp-admin: Download successful, we have the CSV. Thx for the quick action. We'll schedule a change window to enable SCIM early next week.

jess_support: Closing loop: SUP-4982 resolved externally; awaiting customer confirmation on SCIM enablement. Marking thread as 'action required' for identity team to follow up. cc @ivan_identity @kate_sre
